Packages ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) # data wrangling and visualization library(tidymodels) # modeling ``` ::: ## Today's data {.smaller} 2026 House results and projections from Decision Desk HQ (as of 2026-11-04, 11:14 am), merged with 2024 results (from the `gerrymander` dataset we worked with earlier in the semester): ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} midterm_26_raw <- read_csv("data/midterm-2026-11-04-11-14.csv") ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} glimpse(midterm_26_raw) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Rows: 443 Columns: 18 $ district "AK-00", "AL-01", "AL-02", "AL-03", "AL-04", "AL-05", "… $ state_abb "AK", "AL", "AL", "AL", "AL", "AL", "AL", "AL", "AR", "… $ state "Alaska", "Alabama", "Alabama", "Alabama", "Alabama", "… $ house_rep_20 "Don Young", "Jerry Carl", "Barry Moore", "Mike Rogers"… $ house_party_20 "Republican", "Republican", "Republican", "Republican",… $ house_rep_22 "Mary Sattler Peltola", "Jerry L Carl", "Barry Moore", … $ house_party_22 "Democrat", "Republican", "Republican", "Republican", "… $ house_rep_24 "Nick Begich", "Barry Moore", "Shomari Figures", "Mike … $ house_party_24 "Republican", "Republican", "Democrat", "Republican", "… $ harris_24 41.41, 21.89, 53.52, 26.18, 15.96, 34.20, 29.68, 61.45,… $ trump_24 54.54, 76.94, 45.31, 72.71, 83.02, 64.02, 68.47, 37.50,… $ gerry_22 NA, "F", "F", "F", "F", "F", "F", "F", "C", "C", "C", "… $ gerry_24 NA, "B", "B", "B", "B", "B", "B", "B", "C", "C", "C", "… $ gerry_26 NA, "B", "B", "B", "B", "B", "B", "B", "C", "C", "C", "… $ rating_26 "Lean R", "Safe R", "Lean R", "Safe R", "Safe R", "Safe… $ leader_26 "Republican", "Republican", "Democrat", "Republican", "… $ margin_26 9.00, 18.00, 8.00, 28.00, 50.00, 7.00, 15.00, 39.00, 35… $ called_26 "uncalled", "called", "called", "called", "called", "ca… ``` ::: ::: ## Data prep {.smaller} - A seat flips to Democrat if it was held by a Republican after 2024 and a Democrat leads in 2026: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # fmt: skip midterm_26 <- midterm_26_raw |> mutate( flip_dem_24_26 = case_when( called_26 == "uncalled" ~ NA, called_26 == "called" & house_party_24 == "Republican" & leader_26 == "Democrat" ~ "1", called_26 == "called" & house_party_24 == "Republican" & leader_26 == "Republican" ~ "0", called_26 == "called" & house_party_24 == "Democrat" ~ "0", ), flip_dem_24_26 = as.factor(flip_dem_24_26) ) |> filter(!is.na(called_26)) ``` ::: - Data split: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} midterm_26_called <- midterm_26 |> filter(called_26 == "called") midterm_26_uncalled <- midterm_26 |> filter(called_26 == "uncalled") ``` ::: ## Goal {.smaller} Predict whether a seat flips to Democrat based on Trump's 2024 vote share for uncalled seats, using data from called seats. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} ggplot( midterm_26, aes(x = trump_24, y = flip_dem_24_26, fill = flip_dem_24_26) ) + geom_jitter( shape = "circle filled", height = 0.2, alpha = 0.7, size = 3, show.legend = FALSE, color = "white" ) + scale_fill_manual( values = c("0" = "darkgray", "1" = "#0015BC"), na.value = "#A3B18A" ) + scale_x_continuous( limits = c(10, 90), breaks = seq(0, 100, 10), labels = label_percent(scale = 1) ) + labs( x = "Trump's 2024 vote share (%)", y = "Flipped to Democrat", title = "2026 House elections", caption = "Data from Decision Desk HQ, as of 2026-11-04 at 11:14 am" ) + facet_wrap(~called_26, nrow = 2, scales = "free_y") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](20-logistic-regression-II_files/figure-html/flip-plot-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Fitting a logistic model ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} flip_fit <- logistic_reg() |> fit(flip_dem_24_26 ~ trump_24, data = midterm_26_called) tidy(flip_fit) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 2 × 5 term estimate std.error statistic p.value 1 (Intercept) -3.48 0.648 -5.37 0.0000000805 2 trump_24 0.0244 0.0117 2.08 0.0372 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note .fragment} ## Remember In logistic regression, we predict the log odds of the probability of success, $\log\left(\frac{\hat{p}}{1-\hat{p}}\right)$. ::: ## Output $\rightarrow$ model - Output ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tidy(flip_fit) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 2 × 5 term estimate std.error statistic p.value 1 (Intercept) -3.48 0.648 -5.37 0.0000000805 2 trump_24 0.0244 0.0117 2.08 0.0372 ``` ::: ::: . . . - Fitted model: $$ \log\left(\frac{\hat{p}}{1-\hat{p}}\right) = -3.48 + 0.0244\times trump\_24 $$ ## The intercept {.smaller} - If `trump_24 = 0`, then $$ \begin{aligned} \log\left(\frac{\hat{p}}{1-\hat{p}}\right) &= b_0 + b_1 \times 0 \\ &= b_0 \\ \end{aligned} $$ . . . - Exponentiating both sides: $$ \begin{aligned} e^{\log\left(\frac{\hat{p}}{1-\hat{p}}\right)} &= e^{b_0} \\ \frac{\hat{p}}{1-\hat{p}} &= e^{b_0} \end{aligned} $$ ## Interpreting the intercept {.smaller} $$ \log\left(\frac{\hat{p}}{1-\hat{p}}\right) = -3.48 + 0.0244\times trump\_24 $$
. . . $$ e^{-3.48} = 0.03 $$ . . . - Seats where Trump got 0% of the vote in 2024 are predicted, on average, to have a 3% odds of flipping to Democrat. - Since Trump's vote share in called seats ranges from 10.6% to 83%, so this is an extrapolation and not meaningful. ## The slope I 1. Find log odds when the predictor is equal to $x$: $$ log(odds_1) = {b_0} + {b_1x} $$ . . . 2. Increase $x$ by one unit and find log odds when the predictor is equal to $x + 1$: $$ log(odds_2) = {b_0} + {b_1(x + 1)} $$ ## The slope II {.smaller} Difference between the two log odds: $$ \begin{aligned} log(odds_2) - log(odds_1) &= ({b_0} + {b_1 (x + 1)}) - ({b_0} + {b_1x}) \\ log\Big(\frac{odds_2}{odds_1}\Big) &= b_0 + b_1x + b_1 - b_0 - b_1x \\ log\Big(\frac{odds_2}{odds_1}\Big) &= b_1 \end{aligned} $$ ## The slope III {.smaller} Difference between the odds, by exponentiating both sides: $$ \begin{aligned} log\Big(\frac{odds_2}{odds_1}\Big) &= b_1 \\ \frac{odds_2}{odds_1} &= e^{b_1} \end{aligned} $$ ## Interpreting the slope {.smaller} $$ \log\left(\frac{\hat{p}}{1-\hat{p}}\right) = -3.48 + 0.0244\times trump\_24 $$
. . . $$ e^{0.0244} \approx 1.02 $$ . . . Seats where Trump's 2024 vote share was one percentage point higher are predicted to have **odds** of flipping to Democrat that are **higher** by a factor of $e^{0.0244}\approx 1.02$, on average. # Classification
(prediction by another name...) ## Predict {.smaller} ::: question How well did our model do for predicting already called house seats? ::: ::: fragment ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} midterm_26_called_aug <- augment(flip_fit, new_data = midterm_26_called) midterm_26_called_aug |> count(flip_dem_24_26, .pred_class) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 2 × 3 flip_dem_24_26 .pred_class n 1 0 0 353 2 1 0 38 ``` ::: ::: Terrible! ::: ::: {.question .fragment} Is that surprising? ::: ## Predict for uncalled seats {.smaller .scrollable} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} midterm_26_uncalled_aug <- augment(flip_fit, new_data = midterm_26_uncalled) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # fmt: skip midterm_26_uncalled_aug |> select(district, trump_24,
